entries.headline: クワイエット急行909号室: STUDIO909 releases its looping-train mystery demo on Steam
entries.summary: AUTOMATON reports that STUDIO909 has released a Steam demo and new trailer for its mystery adventure set on a train repeating a seven-day journey. Players seek the supposedly nonexistent Room 909. The full game is planned for 2027.

entries.headline: The Blood of Dawnwalker previews update 1.1 for the following week
entries.summary: IGN reports that Rebel Wolves plans The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.1 for the following week, adding directional animal petting, a respec item, an easier mode and subtitle-size options, alongside over 1,100 improvements and fixes. This is an update preview, not confirmation of deployment.

entries.headline: Coral Island plans a Switch 2 release and update 1.4 this winter
entries.summary: Gematsu reports that publisher Balor Games and developer Stairway Games plan to release Coral Island on Nintendo Switch 2 this winter alongside update 1.4, Kids Grow Up. The update expands children’s growth and family interactions. No exact date was supplied.

entries.headline: Order of the Sinking Star sold 45% more Steam units in its first week than The Witness
entries.summary: AUTOMATON relayed Jonathan Blow’s figures showing that Order of the Sinking Star sold 45% more units on Steam in its first week than The Witness did in its Steam launch week. Blow also noted that the new game cost 25% less. The comparison is not an all-platform total or a 45% revenue increase.
entries.verification: The opened AUTOMATON article quotes the developer’s Steam comparison. The verified title registry supplies only the Chinese name.
entries.timeNote: Timestamp is the report publication time recorded in the original evidence packet, not necessarily when the underlying event occurred.

entries.headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4: IGN finds Modern Warfare 4’s campaign a marked improvement in single-player mission design
entries.summary: IGN’s campaign review praised missions built for single-player and the variety provided by its two narrative strands, while finding some character and villain development lacking. The review covers the campaign only; DMZ and multiplayer reviews are separate. No score was present in the packet excerpt.
entries.verification: These are the outlet’s campaign impressions, not a review of every mode. No score has been inferred.
entries.timeNote: Timestamp is the report publication time recorded in the original evidence packet, not necessarily when the underlying event occurred.

entries.headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4: Modern Warfare 4 narrative director gives an ambiguous answer on Captain Price’s fate
entries.summary: In an IGN interview about Modern Warfare 4’s ending, Infinity Ward narrative director Jeff Negus said the team deliberately paced and presented character deaths and that the relevant scene was consistent with others. He did not directly confirm whether Price had died. This summary preserves that ambiguity without detailing the ending.
entries.verification: Based on the developer’s interview quoted in the packet. The reporter’s interpretation is not presented as official confirmation.
